newsitem.title: IRAN: Second jolt hits quake-stricken Iran region.
newsitem.headline: Second jolt hits quake-stricken Iran region.

text.p: A second earthquake struck Iran's devastated eastern region two days after a huge killer quake left some 2,400 people dead, Iran's official news agency IRNA said on Tuesday.

The new jolt late on Monday struck with a force of 4.8 on the Richter scale as rescue teams still searched through the rubble of 200 villages in Iran's northeastern province of Khorasan levelled by Saturday's 7.1 magnitude quake.

There was no word of casualties from the latest tremor, recorded at 8:58 pm (1628 GMT) by the Geophysics Institute of Tehran University which registered the epicentre 850 km (530 miles) southeast of the base, in the vicinity of Qaen.
Earthquakes of force four or more are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area.
Nearly 200 aftershocks have hit Qaen and the nearby town of Birjand with magnitudes ranging from 3.0 to 5.5 since Saturday, IRNA said.
The death toll has remained static at around 2,400 since Sunday but it seemed inevitable that it would rise as relief efforts continued amid the ruins of mud-brick buildings.
Some 6,000 people were injured and tens of thousands made homeless by Saturday's quake.

Another force 4.8 quake hit northwest Iran on Monday in a region still trying to recover from a 5.5 magnitude jolt in February in which Iranian reports at the time said about 1,000 people were killed and 2,600 injured.
